title: Ponce de León finds La Florida, 1513
summary: Three ships left Puerto Rico in early March 1513 with 65 people, among them two free Africans, one of them Juan Garrido, and Antón de Alaminos as chief pilot. They went north-west through the Bahamas, named La Florida at Easter, fought a current that was the first known European meeting with the Gulf Stream, ran the Keys and the Gulf coast against the Calusa, and reached Puerto Rico again on 19 October. Where they first landed is disputed.

legs.source: Wikipedia, Juan Ponce de León: by the Bahamas; the course is the one the winds suggest
legs.note: The landing is disputed: St Augustine, Ponce de León Inlet, Melbourne Beach and a beach north of St Augustine have each been argued. The mark stands at St Augustine

legs.source: Wikipedia, Juan Ponce de León: Herrera, whose 1601 account rests on the ships' logs
legs.note: South along the coast against the Gulf Stream

legs.source: Wikipedia, Juan Ponce de León: the Keys from 15 May, the Calusa coast from 23 May
legs.note: The Gulf-coast landing is most often put at Charlotte Harbor; Tampa Bay, Pensacola, Cape Romano and Cape Sable have also been argued

legs.source: Wikipedia, Juan Ponce de León: Cuba's north-east shore, then Puerto Rico on 19 Oct
legs.note: The sources read give the places and dates, not the way; the line is drawn straight home and does not take in the meeting off Grand Bahama on 8 Jul

events.label: La Florida named
events.text: Ponce de León named the land La Florida, partly for the Easter season (Pascua Florida), and the party came ashore the next day. Where is argued: St Augustine, Ponce de León Inlet, Melbourne Beach, or a beach north of St Augustine. Spanish slavers had raided the Bahamas since 1494 and the 1502 Cantino map may already show Florida, so he was probably not the first European there.

events.label: A current that holds the ships back
events.text: A strong current pushed the ships backward and the smallest, the San Cristóbal, was lost for two days: the first known European meeting with the Gulf Stream.

events.label: The Keys named Los Mártires
events.text: Sailing along the Keys from 15 May, Ponce de León called them Los Mártires.

events.label: The Calusa turn the ships away
events.text: On the Gulf coast the Calusa drove the ships off and relations turned hostile. On 5 June about eighty Calusa warriors faced eleven Spanish sailors and neither side attacked. Charlotte Harbor is the likeliest place, but it is not certain.

events.label: Dry Tortugas
events.text: The ships reached the Dry Tortugas, then steered for Cuba and struck its north-east shore, having underestimated the eastward current.

events.label: Grand Bahama: a ship met
events.text: At Grand Bahama Ponce de León met the ship of Diego Miruelo, whose errand, slaving or spying for Diego Colón, is unclear. His own ship reached Puerto Rico on 19 October; the Santa María came in on 20 February 1514.
